errors.english: those beams, which individually lack the capacity to support the pillar
errors.why: The Tibetan speaks of those (bearers) who individually lack the capacity to lift the beam; the beam is the patient, not the agent, and there is no pillar.

fix.find: those beams, which individually lack the capacity to support the pillar
fix.replace: those [bearers], who individually lack the capacity to lift the beam

errors.english: the inference that determines the other parts is a sign established by direct perception
errors.why: The inference is not itself the sign; it arises (next side) from a sign whose relation (sambandha) is established by perception, and the 'relation' is dropped.

note: Follows the commentary's lemma-gloss pattern reasonably, but the beam example is garbled and the closing doctrinal statement is misconstrued.

errors.english: these phenomena are neither without afflictions nor are they possessed of afflictions
errors.why: The sutra says these dharmas ARE free of afflictions; they are not afflicted.

fix.find: these phenomena are neither without afflictions nor are they possessed of afflictions
fix.replace: these phenomena are without afflictions; they are not possessed of afflictions

note: Good rendering of the Akṣayamati quotation apart from one inverted statement.

errors.english: Therefore, since arising through an intrinsic nature is not illogical, it is merely an object of observation.
errors.why: The Tibetan says arising by own-character is NOT tenable merely on the ground that something is observed.

fix.find: Therefore, since arising through an intrinsic nature is not illogical, it is merely an object of observation.
fix.replace: Therefore, arising by way of an intrinsic character is not tenable merely because something is observed.

note: Generally sound Madhyamaka commentary translation with one sentence whose sense is inverted.

errors.english: This is exactly as it has been taught.
errors.why: These words open the prose commentary on the verse (by the very meditation as taught...), not a third line of the quoted verse.

note: Faithful rendering of the Akṣayamati quotation and the vāsanā argument; only the side-final segment is mis-framed.

errors.english: does not become an object of the path of seeing
errors.why: In this Sāṃkhya verse (guṇānāṃ paramaṃ rūpaṃ na dṛṣṭipatham ṛcchati) mthong ba'i lam is dṛṣṭipatha, 'range of sight', not the Buddhist darśanamārga; same error recurs for the gardens.

fix.find: does not become an object of the path of seeing
fix.replace: does not come within the range of sight

errors.english: is the Primal Nature [note: Sanskrit: (Prakṛti)], yet it is also extremely hollow
errors.why: The Tibetan does not identify the visible gardens with Prakṛti; it says what comes within sight is extremely hollow (and so too, by implication, the pradhāna).

note: The argument about manifest effects and capacity is followed well; the verse's 'range of sight' is mistranslated as a Buddhist path term.

errors.english: Through the pride of the lord of men [note: original Sanskrit: "na vi mā nena", referring to a king]
errors.why: Continuing ma bkur pa (Skt. vimānena) from the previous side: through that humiliation the king's face lost its beauty; it is not the king's pride, and the note misreads the Sanskrit.

fix.find: Through the pride of the lord of men [note: original Sanskrit: "na vi mā nena", referring to a king]
fix.replace: Through that humiliation (Skt. vimānena), the lord of men

note: Readable and largely accurate verse rendering, opening line misconstrued.

errors.english: It is because one intends to communicate in such a way
errors.why: brda byed pa is the convention-maker, i.e. the maker of the mantra (glossed so on the previous side); it is his intention that fixes the result, not a generic 'one's' intent to communicate.

errors.english: transforming the mental continuum [note: original: (saṃtāna) the stream of consciousness]
errors.why: The continuum transformed is that of the mantra (successive distinctions produced in it), not a mental stream of consciousness.
The clause sets up the alternative that the application manifests the mantras (taken up in the next sentence), not a claim that mantras are unmanifest.

note: Argument against Mīmāṃsā mantra efficacy is mostly followed; a few referents in the mantra discussion are misidentified.

errors.english: it would not reside in both one line of text partially obscured or broken at the margin.
errors.why: The Tibetan ends simply 'not ... in both'; the remark about an obscured line is unmarked editorial text inserted into the translation.

fix.find: it would not reside in both one line of text partially obscured or broken at the margin.
fix.replace: it would not reside in both

errors.english: the possessor of conjunction (shaktimat) the entity characterized by the quality
errors.why: ldan pa can is saṃyogin, the possessor of conjunction; śaktimat ('possessor of capacity') is a different term.

fix.find: the possessor of conjunction (shaktimat) the entity characterized by the quality

note: Sound handling of the svabhāva/kārya restriction and the saṃyogin objection, marred by a wrong Sanskrit equivalent and an intruding apparatus remark.

errors.english: the regional governor [note: literally: "the one who holds the portion," likely referring to a local official or the previous ruler]
errors.why: Dum bu 'dzin pa is the proper name of the brahmin antagonist (the Khaṇḍahāla figure of the Candrakumāra story), not a title for a governor or previous ruler.

fix.find: the regional governor [note: literally: "the one who holds the portion," likely referring to a local official or the previous ruler]
fix.replace: Khaṇḍadhara [note: Tib. dum bu 'dzin pa, a proper name]

errors.why: The verb completes the previous side's sentence about sons being born to the thirty-four other queens; plural sons, not Moon.

errors.english: For though men may be born of a great lineage, some are seen to be equal to dogs;
errors.why: The inserted gnomic stanzas (long-metre and four-line verses) are run together as prose, losing the verse boundaries.

note: Narrative is followable but the antagonist's name is turned into a title, and the verses are flattened into prose.
